plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my bid and value. With value $9, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values uniform on [0,49]. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you always pay only that competing bid, never your own. Bidding above value risks losing money on wins; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Since this is a single round with no repeated learning needed, the optimal action is simply to bid exactly my value of $20.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. With value $20, I should bid exactly $20 to maximize expected profit.
